newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan dealer plans to sell 46,000 Opels in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Japan dealer plans to sell 46,000 Opels in 1996/97.

text.p: Japanese foreign car dealer Yanase & Co Ltd said on Wednesday it plans to sell a record 46,000 cars made by Adam Opel AG, the German unit of General Motors Corp, in Japan in its fiscal year to the end of September 1997.
Yanase estimated it would sell a record 39,500 Opel cars in 1995/96, up about 40 percent from a year earlier.
Yanase said it would introduce the Vita Swing, the cheapest version of the Vita compact model, on October 7 at a price of 1.44 million yen.

Of the projected total sales in 1996/97, Yanase said it plans to sell 20,000 Vitas, up from an estimated 15,800 in 1995/96, and 11,200 Vetra medium-class luxury sedans, up from 4,300 in 1995/96. Yanase introduced the remodelled Vetra in April this year.
Yanase also said it plans to launch the Vetra Wagon, a station wagon, in the spring of 1997.
